title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: What is applied is what is reported
summary: Asking once means building the edit twice, and the report was reading the first build. A file that moved while the dialog was open produced an empty edit and no message at all.

highlights.title: No more silent empty edit
highlights.description: The dialog gives the workspace time to move. A file that moved is skipped by the second build, so the command sent an empty edit while its message described the first draw. Counts and edit come from the same build now.

highlights.title: Apply all says what it deletes
highlights.description: That path skips the preview, which was the only place file deletions were visible. The number of files deleted outright is written into the question, before the click.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: The workspace sweep and the removal of code kept alive by its tests report the build they actually send, not the one used to ask the question.
The dialog names how many files Apply all deletes outright.

sections.heading: Notes
bullets: Written down as a test that drives the command end to end with a document whose text changes the moment the dialog is answered.
